VERS. 3.-- *Exspoliavi me.* Ecclesia non inobediens de injuncto officio, sed metuens in assumenda fratrum cura, ne corruat in peccata, sine quibus non [1153C] transigitur haec vita, respondet: *Exspoliavi me.* Quomodo fieri potest ut de culmine contemplationis egrediens, rursus mundi sordibus polluar, quia recepta sollicitudine temporalium subsidiorum, quamlibet eximius doctor, difficile vitat peccatum. [n: (GREG.)] Qui ad sollicitudinem regendarum animarum se accingit, restat ut quibus aeterna praedicat, ad providenda quoque eis temporalium necessitatum subsidia invigilet.

VERS. 4.-- *Dilectus meus.* Ecclesia timente casum, quia Dominus amorem erga se nostrum, in proximorum maximo amore vult cognosci, apte subditur: *Dilectus meus,* quasi: Pertimesco quidem saeculi conversationem; sed intelligo, quod charitas operit multitudinem peccatorum; et confido in dilecti mei auxilio, a quo jam sunt compuncta corda eorum. [1153D] *Manum suam.* Operantem compunctionem, vel, ad memoriam nostram reduxit operationem, quam operatus est in nobis, quia nullius egens, de sinu patris egrediens, in terra pro nobis conversari voluit. *Manum suam* mittit, cum virtute sua animum per subtilem intellectum pulsat. *Et venter.* Potest per ventrem intelligi mollities et fragilitas illorum qui praedicationis officium suscipiunt, quia se minus idoneos recognoscunt, et timent. *Venter.* Id est molles et fluxa pars inter nos; vel, ventris nomine cor designatur, qui sicut cibi in ventre, ita cogitationes in corde excoquuntur. Cor contremiscit, si facere recusat pro proximis, quod Deus fecit pro inimicis. Et venter intremiscit, quia infirmitas gaudens [1154A] de coelesti intellectu in sua exsultatione turbatur, et timet ne perdat, quod tenere nescit.

VERS. 5.-- *Surrexi, ut aperirem.* Surrexi a dormitione ad laborem; quia necesse est ut qui veritatem praedicare disponit, prius ad agenda ea quae praedicat assurgat, ne aliis praedicans ipse reprobus efficiatur; cui subjuncta verba conveniunt, *Manus meae distillaverunt,* etc. *Et digiti mei pleni sunt myrrha.* Digiti, id est discretio, ut solo contuitu supernae retributionis, non pro humano commodo ostendantur operari. Sicut enim in manu sunt discreti digiti: sic in operibus oportet discretionem adhiberi, alioquin non valent.

VERS. 6.-- *Pessulum ostii.* Causam peccati, id est incredulitatem, et quamlibet aliam: quia ut pessulum, [1154B] ostium; sic causa detinet peccatum, qua remota removetur, et sublato peccato patet via Christo. Dixerat, quia dilectus manu missa per foramen se tetigerit ac tremore concusserit: cujus tactu vehementer inflammata, cupit jam non per angustiam foraminis ejus manu contingi, sed patefacta cordis janua felicissimo ejus amplexu perfrui, id est suavitate divinae illustrationis, quam raptim senserat, plenius satiari, sed quia nulli electorum in hac vita conceditur perfecta visio aeternorum, quae in alia vita reservatur, subditur recte: *At ille declinaverat. Anima mea,* etc. Ecce jam tertius gradus: primitiva fuit ex Judaeis conversa; per quam, et postquam haec gentilis, de qua hactenus actum est; quae Gentilis ut diximus, hanc tertiam instituit, de qua modo [1154C] exsequitur: quae usque ad novissimam intrationem reliquiarum Israel durabit successu praelatorum et subditorum. Transi quidem, sed tamen locutus est mihi mandata sua relinquens, ut patienter eum exspectarem: et postquam locutus est, *Anima mea liquefacta est. Quaesivi et non inveni illum: vocavi,* etc. Vox ejusdem Ecclesiae, quae aperuit, secundum illos quos aperuit: quae prius erat venter vel vox ipsorum.

VERS. 7.-- *Tulerunt pallium.* [n: (GREG.)] Pallium tollunt praedicatores, quando, si quid pompae saecularis residuum erat, ab anima auferunt, vel, si quod peccatum per ignorantiam inerat, detegunt.

VERS. 8.-- *Adjuro vos, filiae Jerusalem, si inveneritis,* etc. Adolescentulae jam ad aliquam cognitionem [1154D] promotae, ad famulos Dei, quos angelicam in terris vitam agere credunt, devote veniunt et eos exorant, ut in tempore suae orationis Domino se commendent. Vos filiae Jerusalem supernorum spirituum, qui jam cum Deo regnant. Vel, per filias Jerusalem possumus accipere etiam inferiores in Ecclesia, quos etiam admonent superiores, ut secum quaerant: quia quod a pluribus quaeritur, quandoque citius reperitur, et, ut ubique charitas dilectionis ostendatur.

VERS. 9.-- *Qualis est dilectus.* Haec sponsa recolens intima conscientiae, expavescit, et pigritiam suam accusans ex humilitate ad laborem festinat, dicens: Obsecro, quia sic adjurasti nos fervore divinae [1155A] charitatis, quam habes, me quoque fac ardere, et salutari admonitione in ejus amore me confirmes. Apta et praeconia virtutum ac potentiae ejus congrua laude decantans, denuo interrogatur, in qualium mentibus ejus soleant vestigia reperiri.

VERS. 10.-- *Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus.* Condigna quaerentibus a parte sponsae responsio. *Dilectus meus.* Primo, mundus et sanctus venit in mundum, postmodum passione cruentus exivit de mundo. Per *candidum,* amorem Divinitatis; per *rubicundum,* carnem passam accipe, ut Deum et hominem notet, et in utroque *electus. Electus ex millibus.* Quia unus Mediator de omni numero angelorum, vel hominum acceptus; unde dicitur: *Hic est Filius meus dilectus,* etc. [n: (Matth. III.)] Quia non est [1155B] *inventus alius, neque in coelo, neque in terra qui acciperet librum [n: (Apoc. V)]*.

VERS. 11.-- *Caput ejus aurum optimum.* Alia translatio: *Crines ejus abietes.* Abies, Graece ἐλατη vocatur. Ude hic elate, non Latinum, sed Graecum videtur. Vel caput, id est Divinitas, quia *caput Christi Deus [n: (Cor. II)]*. *Comae ejus,* id est, cogitationes ejus sanctae et rectae, et tamen stultis despicabiles. *Nigrae quasi corvus.* Despicabiles mundo, quasi illa clamosa et improba avis. Vel, *quasi corvus,* ut nulli sacramenta Ecclesiae committant, donec sibi, vel matri similari videant, vel, quia cum pulchri sunt, se fuisse nigros intelligunt ex natura sua.

VERS. 12.-- *Oculi ejus sicut columbae.* [n: (GREG.)] Solent columbae juxta fluenta aquarum residere, ut [1155C] volantium avium in aqua umbram videant, et sic ungues vitent: sic sancti in Scripturis fraudes daemonum prospiciunt, et ex deceptione, quam attendunt, quasi ex umbra hostem cognoscunt, et fugiunt, quae fluenta plenissima dicuntur, quia de quibuscunque in Scriptura consilium quaeritur, per illam ad plenum invenitur. Potest in rivulis, veteris legis eruditio; in fluentis, evangelica perfectio intelligi: quia praedicatores et nova et vetera proferunt. *Oculi ejus.* Id est, dona sancti Spiritus, quae ipse dat, quae amatores suos, non in coeno more porcorum volvi permittunt, sed in similitudine aquarum claros et perspicuos reddunt, nil tenebrosum habentes. Unde et rivulis et mundis aquis, non stagnis turbulentis comparantur, quia Deum vident, et divinorum charismatum [1155D] luce replentur. Quae charismata, quia sola gratia dantur, subditur: *Quae lacte sunt lotae.* Quia sicut mater sola naturali dilectione lac filiis ministrat, sic Deus sola gratia dona charismatum filiis donat. Quae resident juxta fluenta plenissima aquarum: quia quanto de Deo clarius vident, tanto magis ad altiora cognoscenda intendunt.

VERS. 13.-- *Genae.* Id est, modestia et pietas Salvatoris, quae in illo singulariter refulsit. *Sicut areolae.* Quemadmodum ordinatae sunt areolae ab hominibus exspectantibus odoris suavitatem et aspectus gratiam, ita Mediator in carne apparens, doctrinae modestia et dulcedine delectabat praesentes, attrahebat absentes: *consite a pigmentariis;* hoc est, [1156A] apostolis et prophetis, qui concordi voce, non solum ejus sermones, sed etiam mores sacris paginis descripsere, in futura ejus arcana incarnatione, ex modestia Lazarum flevit, sicut agnus obmutuit, et talia. *Labia ejus lilia distillantia myrrham.* Verba doctrinae ejus *lilia* quae claritatem regni coelestis promittunt, gravia patientibus, *primam myrrham,* quia contemptum voluptatum praedicant.



## CAPUT V. (cont.)

VERS. 14.-- *Manus illius.* Id est, opera Christi: quae enim verbo docuit, opere complevit, ut de doctrina sua mirantes, operibus confirmaret. *Tornatiles,* quia in promptu habet facere quod vult, sicut tornatura caeteris est promptior artibus: et quia in se omnem justitiae regulam tenet, unde dicitur: *Oportet in me impleri omnem justitiam [n: (Matth. III)]*. *Aureae, [1156B] plenae hiacynthis.* Quia virtutes quas in homine gessit, divinitatis gratia perfecit: quae nos ad spem et ad amorem coelestium excitant. Hiacynthus enim aerei coloris est. *Venter ejus eburneus,* id est, fragilitas humanitatis: *eburneus* pro decore castitatis, quia ab omni peccato immunis. *Distinctus,* scilicet, non totus eburneus, nec totus sapphirinus. Sapphirus sublimitatem coelestium significat. *Distinctus* ergo, quia partim humana fragilitas esurie, tentatione, fatigatione, morte, partim divina celsitudo, miraculis, resurrectione et ascensione intelligitur. Sapphirus habet speciem sereni coeli.

VERS. 15.-- *Crura illius columnae,* id est, itinera passionis, incarnationis, quae *columnae* dicuntur propter rectitudinem et firmitatem, quia quidquid [1156C] per eum gestum est, ante tempora a Deo dispositum est. *Fundatae super bases.* Id est super prophetas, quia talis apparuit, qualis praedictus ab illis in divina dispositione legentibus. Vel *bases* ipsa dispositio Dei, quae ordinavit. *Species ejus ut Libani.* Quid per singula ipsius Redemptoris membra laudo, totum brevi comprehendam: quomodo *Libanus* altitudine et amplitudine est insignis; ita Dominus inter omnes qui de terra orti sunt, antecellit. Et sicut ille mons nobilium ferax est arborum, ita ille omnes sanctos in se radicatos extollit et conservat; et sicut *cedrus* pulchritudine, fortitudine, sublimitate, odore, omne decus silvarum antecedit: sic dilectus *speciosus forma prae filiis hominum [n: (Psal. XLIV)]*, quia ipse non accepit ad mensuram, et de *plenitudine ejus omnes [1156D] accepimus [n: (Joan. )]*.

VERS. 16.-- *Guttur illius suavissimum,* etc. Id est, internus sapor et dulcedo verborum Christi, quam pauci gustant: qui autem gustant, amplius esuriunt, Aliter: Sicut per guttur ad labia vitalis flatus, ut loqui valeant, procedit, sic in labiis Domini verba quae dicebat. In gutture vero potest occulta dispositio bonitatis ejus intelligi, qua factum est, ut nobis foras loqueretur. *Totus,* id est Deus et homo; *desideralibis,* non solum secundum divinitatem, sed etiam secundum humanitatem ab ipso initio conceptionis, usque ad triumphum passionis, resurrectionis, ascensionis. *Talis est dilectus.* Quasi: Et necesse est si amas eum, et vis ab eo amari, ut eum intelligas talem, et [1157A] tali affectione ei cohaereas. *Filiae Jerusalem.* Pro decore carminis variantur personae colloquentium: sed eadem Christi Ecclesia notatur et nomine sponsae, et nomine filiarum. Cum ad patriam coelestem suspirat, filia: cum nihil nisi Deum curat audire vel loqui, sponsa dicitur.

VERS. 17.-- *Quo abiit dilectus.* Audita qualitate dilecti, de qua quaesierant filiae Jerusalem, addunt aliam quaestionem: quia enumeratis tot laudibus, quis audiens non concupiscat? et hoc in unitate sanctae Ecclesiae inquiri oportet, in qualium corde potissimum, et in quo genere conversationis Dominus soleat inveniri. *Quo abiit,* non relinquendo eos in quibus erat, sed ubi alios associet, et post alios etiam alios invitet, et sic abire, et declinare dicitur, [1157B] ad modum candelae, quae cum accensa sit, multas alias circumquaque accendit, ipsa tamen nihil patiens detrimenti. *Quo abiit.* [n: (GREG.)] Sciendum, quod Deus, qui ubique est, in loco est, sed localis non est. Locale dicitur, quod circumscribitur secundum partes loci supra et infra, ante et retro, dextera et sinistra. Cum vero angeli et humanae animae loco circumscribi non possunt, longe minus illa incomprehensibilis substantia. Major vero cognitio, quae in praesenti de Deo haberi potest, et secundum ejus sola opera: quia quod altius est, in carne possumus mirificentiam operum Dei subtiliter attendere. *Quo abiit dilectus tuus, o pulcherrima mulierum.* Licet Deus communi modo omnibus rebus insit, praesentia, potentia, substantia, tamen familiari [1157C] modo dicitur inesse, id est, per gratiam, illis, quibus opera sua videntur mirabiliora, qui licet plenam Dei notitiam non habeant, tamen mirificentiam operum Dei acutius considerant.



## CAPUT VI.

VERS. 1.-- *Dilectus meus. Descendit* irrigans fonte baptismi, de alto veniens in humili positos visitavit. Ut nos sursum ascenderemus, Dominus in montem descendit, Moyses in montem ascendit. Cum dixisset. *Descendit in hortum,* addit qualiter sit idem hortus constitutus, qua fruge fecundus, cum dicit, *ad areolam aromatum.* Hortus Ecclesia: hortus quaelibet fidelis anima. *Areola* est mens fidelis, quae disciplina rectae fidei edocta, quasi aequis lateribus [1157D] hinc inde est composita: et quasi solerti fossorio creberrime reversata, et a superfluis graminibus expurgata. Respondet piis sanctorum desideriis ac fructuosis operibus eum delectari, ac perfectos quosque castimoniae virtutibus ad aeterna gaudia colligere. *Lilia colligit,* dum ad perfectorum meritorum candorem pervenientes, de statu ubi erant prius, educit et ad coelestia regna perducit.

VERS. 2.-- *Ego dilecto meo.* Hunc versiculum apponit exaggerando stimulum immensae charitatis, quae interius exardescit. Quasi: In me descendit, in me potes habere formam ejus, quem quaeritis. *Ego nepoti meo et nepos meus mihi, qui pascit inter lilia.*

[1158A]VERS. 3.-- *Pulchra es, amica mea.* Hactenus vox Ecclesiae Dominum suum laudantis et quaerentis: qui quoniam a suis amatoribus non longe est, sequitur quid quaesitus respondeat: et declarat se illis loquentibus adfuisse, et quid loquerentur audisse; devotionemque erga se remunerat digna illorum laudatione. *Terribilis, ut castrorum acies ordinata.* Quia per unitatem charitatis compacta, nullum locum aperit per malum discordiae hostibus, id est, haereticis vel immundis spiritibus. Castra Romanorum terribilia erant, quia totum mundum premebant: sed non erant suavia, quia veram pacem non habebant. In Ecclesia nec terror suavitatem, nec suavitas terrorem aufert: quae in terra coelestem vitam agit, et barbaros diversarum nationum animos [1158B] ad suum ritum trahere satagit. Quae tamen quia necdum faciem dilecti, quam maxime quaerit, cernere meretur: hic subsequenter audit:

VERS. 4.-- *Averte oculos tuos a me.* Quasi: Oculos columbinos tibi dedi, quibus semitas justitiae discerneres: sed tamen in tempore tuae peregrinationis ne quaeras me perfecte cognoscere. *Non enim videbit me homo et vivet [n: (Exod. XXXIII)]*. Ne quaeras in via praemium, quod tibi in patria reservatur. *Quia ipsi me.* Non a desiderio cognoscendi desistas, sed de cognoscendi facultate ne praesumas: unde dicitur, *Magnitudinis ejus non est finis [n: (Psal. CXLIV)]*. *Avolare fecerunt.* [n: (RAB.)] Quo intensius me agnoscere quaeris, eo intensius me incomprehensibilem esse intelligis, et non est tua culpa, si me non cognoscis: [1158C] sed est infirmitas humanae conditionis. *Capilli tui sicut grex caprarum,* etc. Hi versiculi supra positi, et expositi, sed non pigeat nos iterando exponere quod auctorem non piguit scribendo iterare, ut novi aliquid addatur. Ne Ecclesia graviter ferret quod a cognitione dilecti suspenditur, sequitur descriptio, qua assimilatur illi primitivae Ecclesiae Jerusalem, de qua non dubitatur, quin amica Dei fuerit. *Omnes gemellis fetibus, et sterilis non est in eis.* Consimilibus fetibus quia tales alios reddunt, quales ipsi sunt. Vel duplices fetus, opera geminae charitatis, vel, fideles de utroque populo conversi: vel, fides et opus.

VERS. 6.-- *Sicut cortex mali punici, sic genae [1158D] tuae,* etc. [n: (GREG.)] Cum multi mira agunt, ventura prophetant, mundum perfecte relinquunt, coelestibus desideriis ardent : sicut cortex mali punici sanctae comparantur Ecclesiae. Sed haec omnia nihil sunt ad comparationem rei de qua scribitur: *Quod oculus non vidit nec auris audivi,* etc. [n: (Isa. LXIV.)] Unde convenienter subdit: *Absque occultis tuis,* quasi dicat, magna quidem sunt, quae in te non latent, sed valde ineffabilia quae latent.

VERS. 7.-- *Sexaginta sunt reginae et octoginta concubinae,* etc. Reginae et concubinae pariter ad thronum regis accedunt, pariter generant, sed non utraeque diadema regni habent. Reginae sunt, quae intuitu regni coelestis doctrinae inserviunt; concubinae, quae amore temporalium Christum annuntiant. Ideo [1159A] illae sexaginta, quia sola dilectione praeceptorum Dei perfectionem operum habent, quod per multiplicationem duodenarii per quinarium potest intelligi: vel quia quinque corporeos sensus ad regulam apostolicae doctrinae temperant. Octogenarius autem cum in malo accipitur, temporalium curas et implicamenta designat: quia et saeculi cursus quatuor circumagitur temporibus, et mundus ipse quatuor climatibus oriente, occidente, aquilone et austro dirimitur, vel ex quatuor elementis compositus.

VERS. 8.-- *Una est columba mea, perfecta mea.* Quamvis multae et diversae personae, tamen fides una est in eis, unum baptisma, unus Deus, unum opus; non alia ante legem, alia sub lege, alia sub gratia: sed in una pace, uno timore constituta. Mater [1159B] nostra regeneratrix gratia est, quae elegit simplices, et electos custodit et sublevat. Vel mater superna Jerusalem, *quia omne donum optimum desursum descendit [n: (Jac. I)]*, quae superna Jerusalem hoc solum de humana conversatione approbat, quod in unitate suae fidei et dilectionis Deo servire desiderat. *Viderunt.* Magna laus catholicae unitatis, quam et gratia mater, quae genuit, in perpetuum eligit; et filiae, quas ipsa per Spiritum genuit et nutrit, mox viderunt, id est castitatem vitae ejus didicerunt. *Praedicaverunt.* Sive illi, qui vere sunt participes regni; sive etiam illi, qui nomine tenus adhaerent, et si spes eorum sit in terrenis, laude dignam fatentur.

VERS. 9.-- *Quae est ista.* Ecclesia gentium ita firmiter [1159C] instituta, et usquequaque multiplicitate sui diffusa et producta per gradus et successiones suas usque ad novissima tempora, illis novissimis temporibus jam intuens Synagoga, tam bene operatam, operantemque ipsam sanctam Ecclesiam, tam diffusam, tot sapientissimos sine schismate sequi unam fidem: praeterea vivorum et mortuorum miracula, et multa alia Christianae fidei argumenta; jam conjuncta, poenitens, et compuncta, dicit admirative, *Quae est ista,* etc. *Quasi aurora consurgens.* Tunc Ecclesia fit *aurora,* cum mortalitatis atque ignorantiae tenebras funditus amittit. In judicio ergo adhuc *aurora,* sed in regno *dies* erit, ubi plenum visum veri solis habebit. *Pulchra ut luna.* In nocte vitae praesentis, ubi variantur status temporalium, comparatur [1159D] *lunae:* quia nunc clara mundo, nunc despecta; nunc virtutum candore plena, nunc pravorum dehonestata vitiis. In futura beatitudine, ubi idem status erit, *sicut sol* fulgebunt justi. *Terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata.* Habent tales praelatos sibi ordinatos, qui probabilibus sententiis fidem nostram evacuant, et terrorem nobis incutiunt. Quo perfectius ordinem in se virtutum collocat, eo terribilior est Ecclesia aeris potestatibus, vel quaeque fidelis anima.

VERS. 10.-- *Descendi in hortum nucum,* etc. Judaea admirante agones Ecclesiae, et inquirente; ipse sponsus perhibet testimonium Ecclesiae. Vel, dicantur esse verba Ecclesiae, quae annuit Synagogae se laudanti, et continuo insinuat, quae sit sibi causa apparatus [1160A] militaris, respondens ex voce doctorum, ducum videlicet suae spiritualis militiae.

VERS. 11.-- *Nescivi, anima mea.* Dum sic sponsus, vel ipsa Ecclesia, labores suos evangelicos Synagogae miranti praedicat: illa salubri poenitudine compuncta, profitetur se causa profanae caecitatis diutius aberrasse. *Conturbavit me.* Propter evangelicam Ecclesiae praedicationem, per quatuor mundi partes velociter discurrentem, et quatuor rotis fidei innitentem: unde et a quatuor personis scriptum fuit; sed illi quatuor equi eodem spiritu ad bellum unum currum trahunt.

VERS. 12.-- *Revertere.* Synagoga confitente suam tarditatem, Ecclesia consolando et exhortando respondet: quater dicit *revertere,* quia Judaei ubicunque [1160B] modo in quatuor mundi partibus dispersi, in fine sunt convertendi. Vel, *revertere* corpore, *revertere* animo ab errore, ut declines a malo. Iterum *revertere* corpore, *revertere* animo, ut facias bonum, et ne velis esse turbata. Non sufficit reverti voluntate, nisi reversio ostendatur Ecclesiae. *Ut intueamur te,* Ut speciem castitatis cognoscamus, et copulante adinvicem nos Christi amore, unam domum fidei ambae in ipso angulari lapide construamus.



## CAPUT VII.

VERS. 1.-- *Quid videbis in Sulamite.* Dum Ecclesia monet Synagogam, ipse Redemptor annuens hortamentis illius, se effectum daturum promittit. Elias enim et Enoch in illis convertendis non laborarent, [1160C] nisi divinis Scripturis et apostolicis testimoniis certitudinem conversionis eorum haberent. *Quid videbis.* Quasi diceret: Doles de incredulitate Synagogae; sed scias in proximo convertendam, ut in ea jam non appareat infidelitas, sed opera spiritualium agonum, et virtutum. *Quam pulchri sunt gressus.* In praemissis descriptionibus est descensus a superioribus ad inferiora, et superiorum tantum fit commendatio membrorum. In hac commendantur etiam inferiora, et ab inferioribus ascenditur ad superiora; ut ostendatur, quod illa Ecclesia in novissimo, ex illis ante reprobis convocata, habebit tamen membra superioribus non imparia; in qua fit mentio gressuum, quia non in otio futura, sed ad certamen processura, [1160D] primam pulchritudinem ex certamine ostenditur habitura. *Quam pulchri sunt.* Primo operum constantiam et mortificationem voluptatum in ea laudat: *Quam pulchri sunt.* Haec dicens ad laudem ipsius Ecclesiae conjunctae ex dulcedine se convertit, ut Judaei facilius convertantur, et Ecclesia de illis convertendis plus laboret. *Juncturae femorum.* Recte post gressus calceatos, junctura femorum laudatur: quia per ministerium praedicantium perficit unanimis conjunctio credentium populorum. *Monilia.* Mundissima, cum jam non dissentiant hi ab illis, sed in omnibus conveniant: et operum attestatione clarescant. *Quae fabricata sunt.* Quae conjunctio, arte inscrutabilis consilii ordinata est: quis enim novit quare Deus usque ad illud tempus Judaeos [1161A] excaecaverit. *Quae fabricata sunt manu.* Id est, ineffabili largitate firmata conditoris.

*Umbilicus tuus.* Illi etiam inter molles, qui gignunt, etsi mundo licite haerent, tamen bene annuntiant.

VERS. 2.-- *Umbilicus.* Id est, infirmitas nostrae mortalitatis fit *crater,* quando infirmitatem nostram in nobis experti, ut alii per nos recognoscant, laboramus, vel aliquando eleemosynas damus. *Tornatilis,* id est rotundus et perfectus: qui enim ob id dat potum sitienti, vel calicem divini verbi porrigit erranti, ut a Deo remuneratore vel terrenam sapientiam exspectet: hujus crater non est torno factus, quia opus misericordiae, quod fecit, non causa suae fragilitatis erigendae ad Deum fecit, sed terrenam mercedem [1161B] requirit. *Venter tuus.* Venter noster *acervus* est *tritici,* cum memores nostrae fragilitatis, fructus bonorum operum, quibus perpetuo reficiamur, in praesenti vita nobis praeparamus. *Venter tuus.* Quamvis sit inferior gradus, tamen triticea refectio erit Deo, quia in imo multi, in superiori pauci, non tamen dicimus in imo, id est, in peccato. *Acervus.* In imo latior, in summo angustior crescit. Sic et in nostris actionibus, quae quanto altioris sunt meriti, tanto pauciores sui operarios inveniunt. In inferioribus plures sunt operarii. Multi de possessionibus eleemosynas tribuunt, pauci sunt qui possessiones relinquunt. Possunt in *acervo tritici* eleemosynae, quas pauperibus erogamus, intelligi, et bene post *craterem* membra sponsae acervo tritici comparantur, ut [1161C] et potum et panem pauperibus dare signetur, quod et de corporali et spirituali refectione aeque potest accipi. In apertis est doctrina poculum, in mysteriis est panis. *Vallatus liliis.* Cum omnia bona, quae agimus, gratia videndae aeternae claritatis gerimus. Et per hoc insidianti inimico aditum nostri cordis circumquaque obstruimus.

VERS. 3.-- *Duo ubera.* Quia doctores rudium non sua praedicant, sed ex eloquiis utriusque Testamenti sumunt quae ab uno auctore sunt edita: ut ipse unus pastor ex duobus gregibus ovium unum ovile impleat; qui *capreae* comparantur, quia mundum est animal, visu et cursu insigne, et findens ungulam, quod ad discretionem boni et mali pertinet; et ruminat, quod post discretionem est faciendum; gemelli [1161D] propter unam concordiam.

VERS. 4.-- *Collum tuum.* Id est, illi per quos vox exit, et esca in corpus trajicitur, qui sunt *turris,* quia et exemplo vitae muniunt alias, et decorant. In *ebore* enim candor notatur. *Oculi tui.* Qui arcana inspiciunt, ut possint in aperto proloqui, qui fluenta doctrinae auditoribus non cessant, sicut in civitate *Hesebon piscinae* semper aquis abundantes, copiose populo in introitu ipsius civitatis aquam ministrant. Et bene dicuntur aquae esse *in porta* civitatis, quia nemo potest Ecclesiam ingredi, nisi prius aspersus aqua doctrinae et baptismi. Unde in introitu templi Salomonis erat mare aeneum, ubi sacerdotes intraturi lavabant manus et pedes. *Piscinae.* Continentes [1162A] multas aquas sapientiae et doctrinae, ad potandum eos qui erunt in *cingulo moeroris,* persequente Antichristo, quae piscinae sunt in illa plenaria introitione utriusque multiplicitatis, quae erit *filia multitudinis. Nasus.* Cautissimi discretores boni et mali, sicut et per nares odor vel fetor discernitur, quos nulla fallit hypocrisis, et eminentissimum tenent locum. *Sicut turris Libani.* In monte idcirco ad speculandum ponitur, ut hostes, qui veniunt, longe videantur: sic praedicatoris vita semper in alto debet firma permanere, ut incursus malignorum longe prospiciat, ut culpam, priusquam veniat, deprehendat. *Contra Damascum.* Damascus metropolis Syriae, quae multa mala intulit Israeli, et etiam captivavit: per hanc omnis multitudo daemonum, vel nequam hominum [1162B] signatur.

VERS. 5.-- *Caput tuum.* Mens tua, quia regit totum corpus cogitationum, est alta, ut mons per conversationem vitae, et talis mons, qui habet scientiam circumcisionis, non in ablatione carnis, sed superfluitatum cordis. Cochleae maris ferro circumcisae, lacrymas purpurei coloris emittunt, quibus collectis tinctura purpurei coloris conficitur. *Canales,* qui purpuram regis suspiciunt, sunt praecordia fidelium. Lana quae intingitur, ut indumentum regis efficiatur, est humilitas in patiendo, quae *juncta est canalibus,* quando constanti corde virtus humilitatis, et continua Dominici cruoris memoria ad tolerantiam animatur. Semper purpuram veri regis, id est passionem, in memoria habentes, et ad imitandum [1162C] parati, ut cum Christo resuscitentur.

VERS. 7.-- *Statuta tua.* Quia Ecclesia in certamine praesentis vitae gaudia futurae vitae praegustat, subditur: *Assimilata est palmae.* Haec est rectitudo bonae operationis, quae ad terrena despicit incurvari, totam se ad coelestia erigit, et in certamine posita tendit ad bravium, quo finito agone, victrix donanda est palma. In inferioribus aspera est, sed desuper pulchra est, et fructum gerit. Sic Ecclesia in terra asperos tolerat labores, sed sperat in coelo se accepturam praemium. Palma conservat folia: sic Ecclesia, variante saeculi statu, eadem tenet fidei sacramenta. *Ubera.* Id est, magistri, qui pro capacitate audientium suam temperant doctrinam, et unumquemque ad sublimia *ab ubertate domus Dei [1162D] inebriant [n: (Psal. XXXV)]*, et corda exhilarant.

VERS. 8.-- *Dixi: Ascendam.* Quasi diceret: Et quod tales habet doctores, tam discrete praedicantes, non est tui meriti, sed donum meum, quia *ascendi in palmam,* id est, dedi Ecclesiae augmentum virtutum, donec ad perfectum veniat, et *apprehendam fructus ejus;* id est, ita confortabo et multiplicabo virtutes in eis, ut nullo modo possint decidere, donec ad maturitatem perveniant, et per hoc *ubera tua* erunt *sicut botrus* cypri, quia illi, qui parva norunt, si benivole nuntiant interdum potiore sapientia debriabuntur. *Dixi.* Quasi, insistendum est ad conversionem Judaeorum, quia tam pulchra conjunctio est secutura, et quia pro eis maxime passus sum, [1163A] quia eos salvandos provideram. *Fructus ejus.* Fructus Crucis, potest dici resurrectio, et ascensio, adventus Spiritus sancti, et salus mundi: et per haec doctores sunt debriati et confortati. *Et odor oris.* Odor malis, guttur vino comparatur: quia mala, ex novitate, vinum ex vetustate laudem consequitur. Sicut vinum malo praestat, ita praestat praesens allocutio Ecclesiae ipsi famae quam de illa potest audientium sermo disseminare. Odor in gutture, vox praesentis doctrinae. In odore fama absentis designatur: et ideo vino illa propter fragantiam virtutum, haec malis ob suavitatem absentis famae comparatur.

VERS. 9.-- *Dignum dilecto meo.* Verbum, quod in ore meo dilectus posuit, tantae est sublimitatis, [1163B] quod non per alium quam per ipsum sponsum mundo debuit praedicari: quia non est alius inventus, *qui solveret librum,* et ab illo susceperunt alii, Christus quasi potavit, quia, docente divinitate, cito in perfectione scientiae profecit, et libenter passionem sustinuit, membra non eodem modo. Dum sponsus laudat guttur sponsae, illa intelligens in gutture verbum, per quod salus datur mundo, designari: ex magno amore verbum dispensare volens, rapit verba ab ore sponsi, ille vino optimo eam comparavit, haec subjecit, *Dignum dilecto meo. Ad ruminandum.* Non ita facile ad potandum, quod ille prius orans aliis porrexerit, sed cum labore et studio meditandum.

VERS. 10.-- *Ego dilecto.* Totum studium meae [1163C] servitutis et devotionis ad ipsum refero, et in praesenti vita, ne laborando deficiam, me adjuvat: et in fine secum ad gaudia recipiet. Ego prius exsul a Deo, ab omni errore ad Deum conversa sum, ut civis et domestica, et ipse prius humano generi iratus ad me est conversus, naturam meae mortalitatis indutus.

VERS. 11.-- *Veni, dilecte.* Qui assumptam pro me humanitatem in coelo locasti, per praesentiam divinae gratiae visita me: ut in agrum mundi semen verbi tui possim spargere, et villas cohabitationis in unam fidem constituere. *Veni.* Ecclesia videns quod nec ad bene operandum, vel egrediendum per se sufficit, nec in bono persistere, vel auditores quantum profecerint discernere, implorat auxilium. In *agro,* Christiani; [1163D] in *villis,* pagani; in *vineis,* Ecclesiae; in *floribus,* fides; in *fructibus,* virtutes; in malis Punicis, martyrium designatur. In his singulis sponsa dilecti sui praesentiam quaerit.

VERS. 12.-- *Mane surgamus.* Quia nox infidelitatis transiit, et lux fidei apparet, procedens ex matutina resurrectione Christi: ab ipso mane resurrectionis laboremus, in inspirando, et ego praedicando. *Videamus.* Ut ego, qui paedagogus sum parvulorum, possim discernere eos, qui acquisiti sunt, quomodo se habeant, quantum proficiant: ut qualiter nutriendi sint, intelligam. Non est intuendum, si vineae florent, sed si flores ad partum fructum convalescant; quia mirum non est, si quis [1164A] bona inchoet, sed valde mirabile est, si intentione recta in bono opere perseveret. *Ibi dabo tibi ubera.* Id est ubi ad videndas vineas, et mala si floreant, venerimus in tuum obsequium: et facta et dicta meorum praedicatorum exhibebo ad similitudinem sedulae nutricis.



## CAPUT VII. (cont.)

VERS. 13.-- *Mandragorae.* Merito invocat sponsum ad auxilium praedicationis, ubi praedicatores praecipuis flagrant virtutibus. *Portae,* apostoli et eorum successores. *Mandragorae,* id est virtutes illorum, quae sunt aptae medicamentis: quae contra sollicitudines mundi adducunt quietem, quae nauseam verbi Dei excludunt, quae vitia ab hominibus sine dolore excidi faciunt, quae proferunt *mala,* id est Ecclesias, suaviter redolentia in confessoribus, similia malis [1164B] Punicis in martyribus: *dederunt odorem,* quia exemplis majorum minores confirmantur. *Servavi tibi.* Vel servavi, id est intellexi omnia praecepta et testimonia, vel promissiones utriusque Testamenti a te esse datas, vel, omnia poma, id est justos utriusque Testamenti per te solum incarnatum justificatos cognovi.



## CAPUT VIII.

VERS. 1.-- *Quis mihi.* Introducitur Judaea jam inspirata et edocta, et summo desiderio Deum investigat. *Foris.* Intus erat dilectus, dum *in principio erat Verbum:* foris, dum *Verbum caro factum est [n: (Joan. I)]*. *Deosculer te,* etc. Id est facie ad faciem videam, et ore ad os loquar.

VERS. 2.-- *Ibi me docebis.* Tu augebis gratiam in [1164C] me, et ego non ingrata augebo servitium.

VERS. 3.-- *Laeva.* Id est mysterium incarnationis, et dona quae dat in praesenti, erit sub capite: quia per ea sustentata in praesenti contra perturbationes mundanas quiescit, et quodammodo cum eo dormit; *et dextera:* id est futura bona, id est plena ipsius visio, *amplexabitur me,* id est, ita undique circumdabit, ut nullus turbo miseriae possit intervenire.

VERS. 4.-- *Adjuro vos.* Audiens sponsus illam ultimam Ecclesiam, et in praesenti velle dormire, et quandoque requiescere; et videns multos gigni ab Ecclesia, qui alios perturbant; admonet illos, ut a perturbationibus desistant. *Donec ipsa velit.* Donec, completis divinae servitutis obsequiis, ipsa ad communem redire curam humanae fragilitatis necessitatibus [1164D] admonita consentiat.

VERS. 5.-- *Quae est ista?* Judaea in tantam sponsi agniti charitatem exardescente, gentilis admirando et congratulando dicit: *Quae est ista? Sub arbore.* Gentilibus admirantibus respondet, ille, qui est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum: et admonet meminisse gratiae, per quam ipsa erepta est, et aliorum congaudere saluti. *Suscitavi.* Quod fuit effectus magnae benignitatis, quia in illa arbore interius excaecata fuit mater tua, ex quo dixit: *Sanguis ejus super nos, et super filios nostros [n: (Matth. XXVII)]*.

VERS. 6.-- *Pone me.* Ponimus Christum *ut signaculum super cor,* cum ea quae dixit, ita discimus, quasi divinae veraciter sint verba sapientiae. Solemus signum [1165A] aliquod digito, vel brachio alligatum circumferre, quo admoneamur illius rei, cujus frequentiorem habere volumus memoriam. Ponimus, ut signum, super brachium, cum ea quae fecit ita audire et sequi studemus, quasi verae sint exempla virtutis. *Quia fortis est ut mors dilectio.* Post corruptionem matris, apte subjungit de dilectione, ut non ex meritis ostendatur data Ecclesiae. *Ut mors.* Sicut mors separat animam a corpore, sic amor Dei a temporalium amore. *Dura sicut infernus,* etc. Quia nullis hostium tentamentis a nostrae salutis cura revocari potuit: sicut infernus nullis miserorum cruciatibus mitigatur, nec a severitate suae sententiae mutatur. Quanto austerior comparatio, eo acrior zelantis nos Domini commendatur affectus. *Lampades ejus.* Id [1165B] est corda fidelium, in quibus dilectio continetur, ut in vase, sunt *ignis:* quia intrinsecus fervent Dei et proximi dilectione. Sunt etiam *flamma,* quia exterius lucent operibus justitiae. Hae lampades non exstinguuntur in adventu sponsi.

VERS. 7.-- *Aquae multae,* etc. Quia domus, quae supra petram charitatis fundata est, irruentibus fluminibus non potest cadere. *Flumina.* Tentationum, quae vel visibiliter vel invisibiliter tentant corda fidelium. *Si dederit.* Quia ubi abundat amor aeternorum, mox vilescit possessio labentium, recte subditur, *Si dederit homo.* Apostoli, et alii sancti, omnibus dimissis, nihil visi sunt sibi perdidisse, dummodo vera bona possent habere, unde Paulus: *Omnia detrimenta arbitror ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciam* [1165C] [n: (Philip. III)].

VERS. 8.-- *Soror nostra,* etc. O vos ministri et commilitones mei, nova est haec Ecclesia et tenera ad novam dilectionem retinendam. *Soror nostra parva.* Ecclesia, antequam crescat per incrementa virtutum, infirmis auditoribus non potest praebere ubera praedicationis; adulta dicitur, quando verbo Dei copulata, sancto repleta Spiritu, per praedicationis ministerium in filiorum conceptione foedatur, quos exhortando parturit, convertendo parit. *Quid faciemus sorori,* etc. Ac si aperte dicat: Parva quidem numero est Ecclesia gentium, et necdum ad subeundum verbi ministerium sufficit. Quid ergo tibi videtur, o Synagoga, erga curam ejus, sororis videlicet nostrae, esse faciendum tempore illo, quo [1165D] illam per apostolos meos, apostolorumque successores alloqui coepero? Utrum quasi parvulae adhuc, parva illi secretorum coelestium arcana committamus, an jam majorem eam per augmenta reddamus, quatenus bene proficiens, perfectiorum possit capax esse virtutum? Cui tacenti, et quid ipse velit potius auscultanti, continuo quid fieri deceat aperit, ita subjiciens:

VERS. 9.-- *Si murus est,* etc. Si inventus fuerit aliquis, qui ab incursionibus errantium possit alios defendere, armis nequitiae fortiter resistendo, vel naturae ingenio munitus, vel philosophica scientia imbutus: divinis Scripturis eum informemus. *Si ostium.* Si quis est non adeo imbutus ad repellenda [1166A] haereticorum sophismata, sed tamen simplicitate fidei, intrare volentibus in atria patriae coelestis, potens pandere rectam viam praedicando, et parvulos imbuendo: proponamus ei immarcessibilia priorum virorum exempla, quibus suum melius impleat officium.

VERS. 10.-- *Ego murus.* Jam loquitur communiter de tota Ecclesia ex apostolorum fundamento incepta, quia extunc fuerunt ubera in Ecclesia, usque ad novissima tempora. *Ego murus.* Audiens Ecclesia haec consilia, vel promissa sui Redemptoris, jam non alter alterum exspectat, sed quisque pro se respondet voce devota. *Ex quo.* Haec omnia non a me habere potui, sed ex quo mihi donum suae pacis, per verbum suae reconciliationis largitus est. *Quasi pacem [1166B] reperiens.* Bene dico pacem reperiens, quia in ea pace, quam dixi, fuit *pacifico* Christo vinea instituta: quae olim a lege et prophetis est praenuntiata. Quae pax non unam tantum gentem Judaeorum continet, sed habet multos populos de toto mundo collectos, non aliquibus hominum meritis, sed sola pace, quam inter Deum et hominem facere venit: cujus vineae, quia Domino cura est, et quia utile est hominibus, ut ejus participes fiant, recte subditur:

VERS. 11.-- *Tradidit eam custodibus.* Sequitur vox ipsius pacifici, quae ostendit, quantam curam habeat de hac vinea, et quid sua relinquentibus in aeternum conservet, et quid singularis praemii doctoribus ejus disponat.

VERS. 12.-- *Mille tui pacifici.* Pretium perfectum [1166C] quidquid habet. Per *mille,* perfectio; per *argentum,* omne mundanum accipitur: quod quidem aliquando parvum est in te, sed magnum devotione. *Mille,* etc. Eadem perfectio quae per *mille* significatur, etiam per *centum* notatur, quia uterque numerus perfectus, et idem valet *ducenti,* quam si diceret duo millia. *Mille,* etc. Idem est *argentei* et *pacifici:* quia pecunia pro Deo erogata, pacem inter Deum et hominem conciliat.

VERS. 13.-- *Quae habitas in hortis.* Ecclesia, vel quaelibet fidelis anima, in hortis habitat; quae jam viriditate spei et bonorum operum est repleta. Sicca quippe est spes hujus mundi, quia omnia, quae hic amantur, cum festinatione arescunt: *Quae ergo in hortis habitat,* oportet ut sponsum *vocem suam audire [1166D] faciat,* id est in tantum bona praedicationis emittat in quantum ille delectatur, quem desiderat; quia *amici auscultant,* videlicet omnes electi, qui ut ad coelestem patriam reviviscant, verba vitae audire desiderant. *Quae habitas.* Et quandoquidem unicuique apud me reservatur pro meritis praemium, et duplex retributio doctoribus: ergo dum adest tempus merendi, dum differtur dies nuptialis, quantum valet unusquisque, in cultura hujus vineae persistat. *Amici.* Id est angeli, quos adjutores tibi dedi; et spiritus justorum, qui jam cum Deo sunt, et pro fratribus orant. *Fac me audire.* Exigo a te ut habites, nullo tumultu discessura; postea etiam exigo ut vocem tuam me audire facias.

[1167A]VERS. 14.-- *Fuge, dilecte.* Annuens Ecclesia, respondet: Quandiu vis, abesto: differ praesentiam tuam; ego spe longanimi quidquid praeceperis, patiar vel faciam. *Fuge, dilecte.* Non optando loquitur, quis enim oportet eum, quem diligit, fugere? sed memor suae conditionis, illius voluntati consentit. *Fuge, dilecte.* Quasi: Tu quidem, qui ex carne comprehensibilis factus es, ex divinitate tua intelligentiam nostri sensus excede, et in teipso nobis incomprehensibilis permane. Hoc clamat Ecclesia Domino [1168A] spiritu prophetico, postquam mortem et resurrectionem Domini ascensionemque descripsit. Fugere nos dicitur, quando id quod reminisci volumus, non occurrit: quando id quod volumus, memoria non tenemus. *Assimilare.* Ita fuge, ut creberrime per gratiam compunctionis fidelium cordibus appareas; qui sunt *montes aromatum,* quia despectis omnibus cupiditatibus, et purgatis vitiis, amore coelestium tenentur, et virtutum odore fragrant, et bonus odor Christi sunt.

## PREFACE.

[1125D]

Solomon, the son of David king of Israel, published three volumes according to the number of his own names. Of these the first is מִשְׁלֵי *misle,* which the Greeks name παραβολάς, the Latins proverbs, because in it, under a comparative likeness, he shows figures of words and images of the truth: but the truth itself he reserved to be understood [1126D] by the wit of the readers. The second book he called קֹהֶלֶת *coheleth*, which in Greek is called ἐκκλησιαστὴς, in Latin *preacher to the assembly:* because the discourses are directed not only to one man spiritually, as in the Proverbs, but to all generally, teaching that all things which we behold in the world are vain and brief: and for this reason least of all to be sought after. The third book he entitled שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים [1127A] *sir hassirim*: which is turned into the Latin tongue as the Song of Songs. Where, by a marriage song, he mystically sings the joining of Christ and the Church. And it is called the Song of Songs because it is preferred before all songs. As in the law certain things are called *holy,* than which greater are the *holy of holies.* In these three books indeed he composed the disciplines of three kinds, by which one arrives at the knowledge of things. For in the first, ethics, that is, the moral, after this, physics, which comprehends the quality of nature, last of all, the theoric, that is, the contemplative. For in the Proverbs, teaching moral things, he set forth a higher understanding through a certain common usage of speech, and fits the keeping of the commandments and the institution of heavenly doctrine to succinct [1127B] words and to brief sentences. Now Proverbs are such as set forth one matter under other words, which are understood otherwise than they are spoken: they have more in the force of their sentences than in the sound of their words; and these the Greeks call παραβολὰς. Ecclesiastes, examining the natures of things, finds that all things in the world are vain and fleeting, and, the frailty of all things being beheld, admonished that the world be renounced. In the Song of Songs, having gone beyond things visible, and contemplating those things which are heavenly or divine, under the appearance of a bridegroom and a bride he declares the unity of Christ and the Church, and, rousing the soul to the love of heavenly things, calls it on to come to the fellowship of God. But that is not to be thought which is handed down by our hearers, that among the Hebrews this was the practice, [1127C] that they should permit no one to read this book save a man already of perfect knowledge and of a faith strengthened in experience: lest the knowledge should not so much instruct slippery minds as the text should turn them to bodily lusts.

Solomon, that is, peaceable, because in his kingdom there was peace, through which the peace of the Church that was to come was figured, *Idida,* that is, beloved, and it signifies him of whom it is said: *Beautiful in form above the sons of men: therefore God hath blessed thee for ever [n: (Psal. XLIV)]*. Ecclesiastes, that is, preacher to the assembly, and it signifies him who was to speak to men reasonably, and to gather together the Church. According to the number of his names he made three books: the Proverbs, in which book he teaches little ones, not so much in age as in wisdom, concerning an even-minded manner of life in the world, [1127D] that is, how they may lawfully use temporal things; Ecclesiastes, in which he instructs men of riper age unto the contempt of fleeting things; the Song of Songs, that is, this present work, in which he teaches the perfected man concerning the love of God alone, that he may rest between the arms of the Bridegroom. Whence also it is called the Song of Songs, excelling by its own dignity all other songs. For by those vices are shunned and the enemy guarded against: by these we are enriched with virtues, and joined to the Lord. In a like order the philosophers also set down their teachings. First they teach ethics, afterwards physics, and him whom they see to have made progress in these they lead on even to the theoric. The matter, the Bridegroom and the Bride, that is, the Head and the Church. And the manner, with what desire the members cleave to the Head, [1128A] and strive to please him, and what gifts they either receive from him in the present or look for in the future, and with what affection the Bridegroom loves the Church, praising her, and admonishing, and comforting her. The end is the love of God.

Four persons I seem to myself to have found in this work, the Bridegroom and his own companions, the Bride and the maidens with her. Some things are said by the Bridegroom, others by the Bride: not a few by the young maidens, certain by the companions of the Bridegroom. For it is fitting that in the beginnings there be a multitude of maidens with the Bride, a throng of young men with the Bridegroom. Understand the Bridegroom to be Christ, the Bride the Church without spot and wrinkle. But the angels, and those who have come unto the perfect man, understand to be the friends of the Bridegroom. The maidens are the throngs of brides that are beginning, [1128B] which have obtained salvation after a certain measure.

Now out of this book the Gentiles claimed the marriage song for themselves, and a poem of that kind was taken up. If thou wilt ascend to the Song of Songs, it is needful to go forth out of Egypt, that after the passage of the Red Sea, the enemies being drowned, thou mayest be able to sing the first song: *Let us sing to the Lord, for gloriously,* etc. [n: (Exod. XV)]. But because thou art still far from the Song of Songs, walk through the land of the desert spiritually, and thereafter, set upon the bank of Jordan, sing the second song, *Hear, O ye heavens, the things which I speak,* etc. [n: (Deut. XXXI)]. And when thou hast passed through all things, climb up to higher things, that thou mayest be able, a comely soul with the Bridegroom, to sing this Song of Songs also.

It is to be noted that the Bride always longs to abide with the Bridegroom in the house, or in [1128C] the little bed, or in some more inward place: which befits women. He, as is the part of males, calls his beloved out to the outdoor work of the vineyards, or to works of this kind: because doubtless the Church, if it could come to pass, desires to rear up offspring for the Lord in the tranquillity of peace. But he in the present exercises her with frequent persecutions, that she may come the cleaner to things eternal, lest, if prosperous things befall, being delighted with the sojourn of the present world or of her exile, she sigh less after the heavenly country.

Synagogue, a gathering together, which is also of stones: Church, a calling together, which is of rational beings. And each of these, a portion of the just, has been made a partaker in the same faith of Christ and in the same love, at diverse times, the former by awaiting him who was to come, the latter by receiving him present. All [1128D] the motions of the soul, God the founder of the universe created unto good: but by our own use it often comes to pass that things which are by nature good, while we ill abuse them, lead us down into sin. One of the motions of the soul is love, which we use well if we love wisdom and truth: but ill, if flesh or blood. Do thou therefore, as a spiritual man, hear spiritually the words of love of the song that is sung, and learn to carry over the motion of thy soul and the burning of natural love unto better things.



## CHAPTER ONE.

VERS. 1.-- *Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth.* The voice of those who go before the coming of Christ, who pray to the Father of the Bridegroom, that is, of Christ. In the midst of the prayers she is heard, [1129A] and seeing the Bridegroom she speaks to him: Let him touch me with the sweetness of his presence, which I have very often heard promised by the prophets, and, bringing as it were a kiss, let him receive also the touch of my mouth; that is, let him hear me asking concerning the way of salvation, and, making both one, let him bring the kiss of peace. To kiss is put for to be made at peace, after the likeness of those who through discord have departed from their lords, but on returning kiss one another and are perfectly reconciled, so the Synagogue longs that the human race, removed from God by sin, be reconciled through the incarnation of the Son. As many precepts as she learns from his preaching, so many kisses of his mouth, as it were, she receives. She speaks after the manner of one who loves, who for the fervour of her love is not able to keep the order of speaking. For as in a kiss two different bodies [1129B] are joined, so in the incarnation of the Son two substances, of the godhead and of the manhood, utterly different, are united in an inseparable conjunction. *They are better.* She names the breasts of the Bridegroom Christ, which is a woman's thing, that at the very beginning of the song she may make plain that she speaks figuratively. Therefore do I desire the kiss, which is also my redemption; because thy instructions, which are the milk and the nourishment of children, are better than other doctrines, which do not cherish but slay the simple: as wine kills little ones. By the odours of ointments the repute of virtues is wont to be signified.

VERS. 2.-- *Thy name is oil poured out.* Therefore also do I desire the kiss, because thy name is oil, etc. The Bridegroom came anointed from the Father to the Bride, that he might anoint the Bride also. From chrism, Christ, that is, anointed from [1129C] the anointing; which name is poured through the grace of the Holy Spirit in baptism upon all the faithful. I cannot yet embrace thee thyself, meanwhile thy name, out of desire of thee, shall pass the night with me. The name of Jesus came into the world, and straightway is preached. *Oil poured out,* that is, in the whole earth the name of Christ is preached; now the name of Moses is heard among the Gentiles, which before was shut within the narrows of Judaea alone. *Therefore the maidens have loved thee.* Saying these things, she beholds the maidens, who were not present while she spoke before, but in the midst of her prayers the choir of maidens enters in, and is praised by the utterances of the Bride. All the Churches, which make one Catholic Church, are the maidens: not old through fault, [1129D] but new through grace, not barren with age, but by the age of their mind fitted for spiritual fruitfulness. And because with the oil of thy grace thou hast emptied out all the griefs of sins, *Therefore the maidens,* etc.

VERS. 3.-- *Draw me after thee.* The maidens answer: *Draw me after thee.* The Bride does not follow behind his back, but joined to the Bridegroom's side, the handmaids enter in after her. *Draw me after thee.* Thus far the voice of those awaiting the incarnation of the Saviour, and commending his gifts: from here on is brought in the voice of those who came to the faith after the times of the incarnation. The former was asking that he would come and offer a kiss; the latter does not entreat that he should come down to her in that manner any more, but rather she herself desires to follow him to the heavens: and because she sees that this cannot come to pass by herself, she implores the leading of him to [1130A] whom she desires to come. *Into the odour of the ointments.* In the consideration of miracles. *The king hath brought me in,* etc. The Bride, having entered into the inner chamber of the Bridegroom, returns to the young maidens and announces to them: *He hath brought me in.* Or, through hope he has led me into eternal blessedness, in the plural, for the manifold abundance of good things, as if I have already tasted beforehand the sweetness of the heavenly kingdom, and the things which are prepared for me in the heavens I have known by his own revealing: and soon, turned to him who reveals this to her, she gives thanks for his benefits. There are four things in a house: the gate, the ascent, the dining-room, the bedchamber. By the gate we understand faith: by the ascent, hope: by the dining-room, charity: by the bedchamber, blessedness itself. *We will exult and be glad.* As if she would say: We extol not ourselves for the gifts received, but thee: mindful in [1130B] all things with how great tenderness thou hast vouchsafed to soften the austerity of the law by the grace of the faith of the Gospel: therefore not in ourselves, but in thee will we exult, because all the upright love thee, and have learned that thou art to be loved above all things. The Bride having entered again into the inner chamber, the maidens, while they await her coming, joyfully sing together for the Bride's perfection. *Mindful of the breasts.* And *the upright love,* is referred to the commendation of the Bride. *Mindful of the breasts,* etc. She (who is the greater) already enjoys to the full the milk of thy breasts. We also do not indeed love, but we shall love. Then they speak to the Bridegroom, *The upright love thee.* The upright, all who are upright of heart love thee above all things, nor are they upright who set anything before thy love, from whom alone they have whatever of good they have. *The upright love.* In vain do those believe themselves to love [1130C] the Creator, who despise his admonitions. The truly just violate God neither in deed, nor in thought, nor in word.

VERS. 4.-- *I am black.* After the Church has been led into the storerooms, that is, through knowledge and through hope of the good things to come, after she has learned to love him with an upright heart and to rejoice in his grace, it remains to show that for the love of him and for the obtaining of the good things which she has tasted she undergoes a struggle, and what of affliction she bears. *Black.* As if she should say: you promise that you will go with me, and the tribulation which I suffer can deter you: but let neither affliction nor ill fame deter you, because these shall confer the comeliness of virtues, and after love there remains patience for the testing [1130D] of love. *Black.* Again the Bride answers the maidens, and the matter treated is open temptation. *Black.* Vile indeed do I appear in the eyes of those who persecute me, but before God I shine glorious by the confession of the truth. *As the tents of Cedar.* Here *as* is put not for the truth, but for the estimation of the foolish, who think her the dwelling of vices or of demons; *as the skins of Solomon* is here put for the truth. *Cedar* was a son of Ismael, whose hand was against all, and the hands of all against him, having no place among men, but for his wickedness and his wrath dwelling always in tents. So too the just are believed to be driven out and afflicted for their own deserts, and are judged as it were the enemies of all: whence it is said, *You shall be hated by all men for my name's sake [n: (Matth. X)]*. *As feet.* [var: Vulg. Ct 1:4 *sicut pelles Salomonis*, "as the skins of Solomon"] [1131A] The Church, mortifying in herself carnal desires and adorned with virtues, becomes a dwelling worthy of the true peaceable one. Therefore the flesh of the Lord's manhood is called a skin, because as a tent is stretched over a man lest he be burnt by the sun, so the flesh of Christ stretched out upon the cross was for us an overshadowing of vices.

VERS. 5.-- *The sun hath discoloured me.* It belongs to the sun both to burn and to enlighten, so the true sun burns his own outwardly with persecutions, and by giving strength to resist enlightens them. *The sons of my mother.* And she answers as it were to the objection of the weak who doubt: she shows whence she bore the first madness of the persecutors, which appears the heavier for this, that it came from those of her own tribe. *The sons,* that is, the apostles destroyed our sect. Paul the persecutor of the Church was a son of her mother according to the flesh and to his upbringing: [1131B] and doing penance, turned to the standards of his sister, he preached the faith which before he was destroying. *They have set me.* There was one vineyard of Christ in Jerusalem, namely the primitive Church, which on the day of Pentecost was established by the coming of the Holy Spirit, of which at that time the apostles were the keepers: but when persecution arose they were scattered into the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles, and so it came to pass that there were more vineyards, that is, in more places. And while the Jewish persecutors wished to trouble the Church, unwilling they were scattering the seed-plot of the word more widely, and by persecuting one they caused many to be established. When therefore she had said that she was afflicted with the parricidal hatred of the Synagogue, she straightway subjoins how much she profited through this affliction: adding, in the person of those to whom the care of preaching was [1131C] committed: *They have set me keeper in the vineyards.* [n: (GREG.)] Our *vineyards* are our actions, which we cultivate by the practice of daily labour. But being set *keepers in the vineyards,* we keep not our own vineyard: because while we are entangled in outward actions, we neglect the ministry of our own action. While I was keeping many vineyards, that I might gain others, in certain of them I suffered losses. The bitterness of the persecution of the sons of the Synagogue made me not to keep my own vineyard, because, the doctrine of the Gospel being left behind, they were forcing me to the distinctions of the legal observances.

VERS. 6.-- *Show me,* etc. The voice of the Church that is beginning from among the Gentiles, to the Bride, because many false prophets go out into the world, saying: Behold here is Christ, behold there; she entreats that she may be able to discern in [1131D] whose profession and work he may be found. *Show me* my shepherd, whom I love with my whole soul, and in whom he has his rest and his pastures, lest, troubled by the heat of temptations, I begin to seek it through the conventicles of the companions, that is, of the heretics. Or, in the voice of the preachers to the Bridegroom, that they may be able to discern to whom they ought to minister the words of life. Then she beholds the Bridegroom, who, once beheld, went away. And he does this frequently in the whole song, a thing which he who has made trial of it has proved in himself, the Bridegroom, often held, often slips away, until he shall be truly held. *At midday,* etc. That is, in the splendour of thy majesty, which befits the perfect, not in the morning or in the evening. Or, *at midday,* that is, in the burning of tribulations, which the devil sends in, grieving that the world is snatched away from himself [1132A]. The quality of things is wont to be marked from the time. Abraham at midday received the angels. Joseph at midday feasts with his brethren. *Of thy companions.* The heretics are called companions, because they carry about the mysteries of his name and of his confession.

VERS. 7.-- *If thou know not.* Because the Bride, while she was seeking the helps of God's presence in tribulations, had subjoined, in the person of the weak, *Lest I begin to wander:* straightway the Bridegroom, being implored, rebukes that same trembling of hers with a kindly chiding, according to that word of the Gospel, *O thou of little faith [n: (Matth. XIV)]*, as if he should say, thou fearest to be blotted out by me in tribulation, and thou complainest that thou art blackened in the burning heat: but I have appointed to make thee fairer through tribulations. But if perchance thou knowest not this, nor rememberest that no man is crowned [1132B] save he who has striven lawfully, go forth from my fellowship. [n: (GREG., lib. XVI Moral, c. 21.)] She knows her own self when, set in mind among sinners, she remembers that she was made unto the image of her author, and walks according to the order of the likeness she has received; but if she knows it not, she goes forth from the secret of the heart into outward lusts, and, led to the broad way, follows the examples of the peoples. The Lord, chiding the Church that is afraid, admonishes her of the grace given her against the snares of the enemies. *Thy kids.* Because they are trained not according to the rule of my commandments, but according to thy errors. *Beside,* in the footsteps of the shepherds thou shalt be made the last, not among the sheep, but the kids. Or *beside,* that is, that thou mayest be like to the true shepherds, because hypocrites seem to follow good men.



## CHAPTER ONE. (cont.)

[1132C]VERS. 8.-- *To my horsemen.* As I freed the former people from the Egyptian servitude, so will I free thee from the hands of thy persecutors, dashing Pharao in pieces, if thou shalt know thyself to be my bride, freeing thee from the servitude of the devil in the font of baptism reddened by his passion, the author of sin being drowned in that same place. *To my horsemen.* Because the Lord wills not that the Church be ignorant of herself, but that she diligently attend to what of gifts she has received and what she ought to suffer, accordingly after the threat he speaks softly to her, as if he should say: If thou wilt understand how thou oughtest to know thyself, understand to what I have likened thee, and then thou shalt know thyself to be such, through my benefits conferred upon thee, that thou oughtest not to be troubled. *To my horsemen.* The horseman is the Bridegroom, as the prophet says: *And his salvation is a riding [n: (Habac III)]*. [var: Vulg. Hab. 3:8 *et quadrigae tuae salvatio*, "and thy chariots are salvation"] By how much therefore my company of horsemen differs from [1132D] the horses of Pharao, by so much art thou better than all the other daughters. As that people was terrified when the chariots of Pharao came upon them, but was saved by heavenly protection, and, the enemies being drowned, was led through the waters into the land of promise: so the wave of death, which shall meet all mortals, snatches the depraved into destruction, unlocks for the godly the way to salvation, and all the other things which there are done bodily are here fulfilled spiritually. He kindly chides her as she doubts, and lest she despair he manfully strengthens her in the faithful love that follows, where he compares her to the chariots of Pharao. *In the chariots of Pharao.* That is, in the time of the chariots. And mark the pride: Pharao is interpreted *dashing in pieces* or *scattering*. Nor is it needful that thou begin to wander, since thou hast me for a consoler, [1133A] and prelates on whom thou mayest lean, through whom thou mayest stand.

VERS. 9.-- *Fair are thy cheeks.* Since it has been shown how the Lord protects the Church amid adversities, it remains to be shown how great a love of the Lord himself the Church keeps amid adversities. Whence follows, *Fair are thy cheeks.* With so great a power of saving modesty have I adorned thee, that by no doctrine or suggestion of depraved teachers dost thou corrupt the chastity of the faith promised to me, by whom thou wast fearing to be led into error. The beauty of a woman is said to lie for the most part in the cheeks. Allegorically. In the *cheeks* is marked the sign of modesty, as in preachers the habit of living rightly. The Church, although widowed by the death of her Bridegroom, is yet held by so great a memory of him that she can in no wise receive the fellowship of strangers: [1133B] and she groans both for her own sins and for those of others. In the *neck,* the teachers, in the *jewels,* their works: because the things which they teach by word, they also do. He shows, by subjoining, what is the grace of keeping this sobriety. *Thy neck as jewels.* For through the neck we pass food into the body that is to be refreshed, and we utter words by which we declare the secrets of the heart to our neighbours, that is, the teachers, who both instruct by words and pour over the food of salvation into the members committed to them. They are compared to jewels who are fair in manners, and who close up the breasts of virgins with words and examples, lest the adulterer put in his hand.

VERS. 10.-- *Chains.* Another translation. *We will make for thee likenesses of gold with distinctions of silver, so long as the king is upon his couch.* Which is, [1133C] gold, that is, my face thou shalt not be able to see in the present life, but the likeness of the heavenly brightness thou shalt see, through the illumination of the Scriptures, through a glass in a dark manner, until that appear to all which now lies hidden in the Godhead. *Chains.* Beautifully does the Bridegroom describe her beauty: after these things the Bridegroom comes to be with her at the couch. Meanwhile, while he sleeps, his companions, that is, the angels, console her; we have not gold, but we will cause a likeness of gold to be made for thee, until he rise with the marks of silver. *Chains.* Whatsoever good instructions, as it were the ornaments of the ears. In the *chains,* Holy Scripture, which shines within with the *gold* of spiritual senses, and glitters without with the *silver* of heavenly speech; through the edification of teachers there comes to be a keeping of sobriety, and through the [1133D] meditation of the divine Scripture. Shining within and without with the gold of divine wisdom and the silver of divine speech. *We will make.* I and my workmen, whom in great number I have appointed to dispense the seeds of the word.

VERS. 11.-- *While he was.* The Church, having received such great gifts and promises from her founder, makes plain with what devotion of works she received them, saying: *While the king was,* which is, when the Son of God appeared in the flesh, the Church grew up through that very mystery of the incarnation into the fervour of heavenly virtues. Or, when the human race, redeemed by the cross, was in the humiliation of the cross, the exercise of good works sprinkled abroad an odour of sweetness. While Christ the king rests in the blessedness of the heavenly secret, the great virtue of the saints [1134A] in the Church ministers to us the grace of sweetness, who, the more they see not him whom they long for, so much the more ardently do they burn with desire. Or, while he was with the Father, the *nard,* that is, the love wherewith he first loved us, *gave its odour,* because through love he took flesh for our sake. A wonderful order of words. While the king reclined, my nard gave its odour, in that for the exceeding charity wherewith he loved us he was made the son of a woman. *Nard,* which is said to drive out swellings, to put cold to flight and to bring warmth; to which the Lord's manhood is likened, who by taking flesh humbled himself, and by humbling himself took away every swelling of pride, removed the cold of unbelief, and brought in the fervour of charity. This herb also, the more it is bruised, so much the greater odour does it render, so Christ.

[1134B]VERS. 12.-- *A bundle of myrrh.* The death of my beloved, which he underwent for my salvation, shall abide always in my memory. Likewise he is compared to a bundle of myrrh, in that for our sake he bore the injuries of the cross. Myrrh is a tree of Arabia, of the height of five cubits, like to the spike which they call acanthus, whose drop is green and bitter, whence myrrh received its name. Its drop, flowing of its own accord, is more precious, that from a wound of the bark of less worth, which is wholesome for the healing of infirmities: whence also he received myrrhed wine from the soldiers. *My breasts.* The breasts of the chaste are not broken; but those of harlots are wrinkled with slackened skins. Whence Ezechiel: *In Egypt were thy breasts broken [n: (Ezech. XXIII)]*.

VERS. 13.-- *My beloved is a cluster of cypress.* He is a cluster of cypress [1134C] when he rose again: he is *In the vineyards of Engaddi* when he distributes spiritual gifts to the faithful. The balsam trees which grow in Engaddi, because they are cultivated after the manner of vineyards, he calls vineyards. The Bridegroom Christ therefore is in the vineyards of Engaddi, because coming in the flesh full of the Holy Spirit he bestows upon believers the gifts of that same Holy Spirit through the anointing of chrism, in the making of which oil and balsam are mingled together. Engaddi, the fountain of the kid, on account of the graces which after the resurrection he bestowed in baptism upon those who partake of him. Engaddi, that is, the eye of my temptation, and the life of man upon earth is a temptation. Because to the death of the Mediator the glory of the resurrection soon succeeded, rightly is it subjoined, *A cluster,* who was a bundle of myrrh in the bitterness of the passion, and in the sweetness of the resurrection stood forth [1134D] a cluster of cypress. For what myrrh makes sad, wine makes glad.

VERS. 14.-- *Behold thou art fair.* Thus far the Church bears witness what pledges of love she has received from the Bridegroom, to whom he himself soon answers by way of recompense: *Behold thou art fair;* as if, from this, that thou lovest me, thou art made fair. *My love.* Another translation: *My neighbour;* that is, in this, that thou art near, thou art comely, and after thou hast begun to be comely, thou art fair without any addition. *Thy eyes.* Another praise of the comely Bride, that we also may labour to become comely. *Thy eyes are the eyes of doves,* thou lookest upon God simply, because thou seekest nothing else but him. *He that shall look on a woman to lust after her [n: (Matth. V)]*, has not the eyes of a dove; [1135A] but he who has them looks with chaste eyes, and understands both the law and the Gospel spiritually. In the appearance of which dove the Holy Spirit appeared. And therefore both spiritual understanding and all spiritual gifts are designated by the name of the dove. The dove lacks gall, hurts not with its beak, builds its nest in the hollows of rocks, nourishes the young of others, abides beside the streams, chooses the better grains, renders a moan instead of a song, flies in flocks, defends itself with its wings, recovers its sight. So the saints, sitting beside the streams of doctrine, choose the better sentences, nourish unto God men estranged from Christ, and if they find any good sentences among heretics, they do not pervert them, they lack unreasoning anger, they have their refuge in the faith of the wounds of Christ, they groan for their sins.

VERS. 15.-- *Behold thou art fair, my beloved, and comely.* [1135B] The Bride, hearing that through the Bridegroom's love she had deserved to be praised by the Bridegroom himself, renders him a return in praises: not that by her own proclaiming she bestows on him what he has not, but understanding his comeliness, through which she herself also was made comely, she says: *Behold thou art fair,* etc. *Our little bed is flourishing.* Sometimes the Church rests with the Bridegroom as it were in a little bed, that is, in the time of peace, where she beholds the beauty of God more clearly, and begets of water and the Holy Spirit an offspring of the faithful fragrant with the flower of faith. Sometimes, when temptation rises up, she stands with the Bridegroom in the line of battle. Or, the *little bed,* the little ones of the faithful, who are a rest to God and to their masters, by this at the least, that they will not sin mortally, who flourish with the beginnings of good works, whereby they give hope of fruit, that is, of greater works. Wishing to lead a quiet life in [1135C] the Bridegroom, she intimates what manner of houses those are in which she would receive him. The peace of the Church flourishes with virtues and is multiplied with spiritual offspring.

VERS. 16.-- *The beams of our houses are of cedar.* The houses are the various Churches of the Gentiles throughout the world; the *beams,* which are wont to be made for the fortifying of a house, are the preachers, by whose word and example the structure of the Church is held together, lest it fall. The *ceilings,* which are wont to be made for the adorning of a house, are the simpler servants of Christ, who cleave to the beams and are upheld, who adorn not by doctrine, but by virtues. *Of cypress.* The cypress is so called in Greek, because its head rises from a roundness into a point: whence also κῶνος is called a whirling top, that is, a lofty roundness, hence also when the fruit is called a cone: whence, *Cone-bearing cypresses.*



## CHAPTER II.

[1135D]

VERS. 1.-- *I am the flower of the field.* Because in the state of the present time labour rather than rest is fitting: rightly does he call the Bride, who is delighted with leisure, to the exercises of labours. As if he should say: Thou indeed, wishing to render thy beauty commendable to me, delightest to flower in quiet with secret virtues: but know thou that I require another manner of beauty in the present, because I am the flower of virtues, from which every fruit of the field goes forth; because I desire that my odour become known to the whole world, which cannot be fulfilled unless, the quiet in which thou delightest being broken off, thou gird thyself to the office of preaching. And *the lily of the valleys* rather than of the mountains, because I reveal the brightness of my manhood, or the splendour [1136A] of eternal light, or of the Godhead, rather to the humble and to such as are ready to suffer. As if: Remember that I, who could be born of a virgin, who am God, appeared humbly in the world, showed myself to be a companion to men, came humbly even unto death. Therefore cease to seek the security of quiet, whence he subjoins, *As the lily.* As a field is adorned with flowers, so the world is adorned with the knowledge of me and with faith.

VERS. 2.-- *As the lily.* Himself being praised, he praises the Bride, thus: *As the lily* cannot be compared to the *thorns* among which it often springs up: in the same way my neighbour is above all the *daughters a lily.* *As the lily.* Thou seekest rest and the praises of the *little bed:* but know that thou art made whiter by the stings of tribulations, and that the fruit of preaching is greater than the fruit of quiet. *So is my love.* [n: (GREG.)] [1136B] In the Church neither can the evil be without the good, nor the good without the evil: he was not good who could not bear with the evil. By the dogmas of adverse heresies her wholeness is pricked as with thorns, that watching she may be exercised against her enemies, until, standing out as a lily upon the head of her Bridegroom, she be adorned with that very whiteness.

VERS. 3.-- *As the apple tree,* etc. The Bride, being praised and admonished by the Bridegroom's example to suffer, extols the Bridegroom with a praise in return, in that among the works of the good [singulariter] he likewise stands out as holy, and she promises that she will suffer what he suffers, under the presiding of him who is her refreshment and her refection. *As the apple tree.* The odour of ointments, although it smells sweetly, is nevertheless not sweet to eat. But an apple of the best savour and odour is such that it delights the throat with sweetness, and its smell [1136C] soothes the spirit. *Under the shadow.* Therefore do I set my beloved before all, because in the protection of his tenderness alone, for desire of which I was burning, I see that I have found a refreshment of tribulations, and I feel the most sweet fruit of his gifts, whereby I trust that I shall be refreshed for ever. Now she had desired to breathe again *under the shadow* of her author, when she complained that she was darkened by the sun of persecution, when, imploring the help of God, she cried: *Show me whom my soul loveth: where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday;* when, not only wearied with the tedium of oppressions, but allured by the remembrance of his beauty and comeliness, she said: *Our little bed is flourishing;* and she shows that she has been made possessed of that desire, saying: *Under the shadow.* And it is to be noted that above she was proclaiming *beams of cedar and ceilings of cypress,* yet she was not recording that the protection of these [1136D] sufficed for her; but she was seeking the tree of life alone, in whose shadow she might rest and by whose fruit she might be refreshed, because the saints bring their suffrages by examples, by doctrine and by intercession: yet to the Saviour alone have we to say, *But the children of men shall hope under the protection of thy wings [n: (Psal. XXXV)]*. [var: Vulg. Ps. 35:8 *in tegmine alarum tuarum*, "under the covering of thy wings"] *I sat down, and the fruit,* etc. She says not, I sit, but, *I sat down.* Such are the advances of the Churches, that in the beginning a man desires to sit down in the shadow of the virtues, that his body may come to him, from which the shadow is born: therefore also the nativity of Jesus began from a shadow, and is ended in truth. As it is said: *The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee [n: (Luc. I)]*. So afterwards a passage is made to better things.

[1137A] *Sweet.* Because in it the soul understands the cause of life, while it perceives it also bodily.

VERS. 4.-- *He brought me in.* Of how great sweetness, of how great power this refection is, is shown when she subjoins, *He brought me in.* That is, he has so gladdened me with the hope of glory to come that I no longer feel the labours of the world. *He brought me in.* [n: (AMBR.)] As soon as my throat touched the sweetness of his grace, so do I feel myself refreshed in spirit and carried over from the love of earthly things into the things above, as if, brought into the wine cellar, I had been refreshed with the odour and the cup of new wine. Typically by *wine* the grace of the Holy Spirit is marked; the wine *cellar* is the Church, in whose unity alone the Holy Spirit is wont to be given and received; which Church, gathered out of the whole world, God built into one house for himself, and which the Holy [1137B] Spirit consecrated with his own gifts. Which building, because it stands upon the foundation of the greatest charity, by his own working, rightly is it subjoined: *He hath ordered charity in me.* The charity of many is disordered, that which is in the first place they put third or fourth. First, God is to be loved; secondly, parents; then children, afterwards those of the household, who also, if they are good, are to be set before evil children.
